party.label: Party positions
party.note: How far apart the parties stood at each election, weighted by the votes they got. V-Party, 142 countries.

axes.label: Economic left and right
axes.note: Where the party stands on state intervention in the economy.

axes.label: Immigration
axes.note: How restrictive the party is on immigration.

axes.label: LGBT rights
axes.note: Whether the party supports equal rights for LGBT people.

axes.label: Minority rights
axes.note: Whether the party supports the rights of minorities.

axes.label: Religious principles
axes.note: How far the party wants religious principles in public policy.

axes.label: Political pluralism
axes.note: Whether the party accepts that opponents are legitimate.

axes.label: Political violence
axes.note: Whether the party encourages, or refuses to condemn, political violence by its own supporters.

axes.label: Populism
axes.note: How far the party runs on a pure people against a corrupt elite.

axes.label: Anti-pluralism
axes.note: How far the party rejects the rules that let it be voted out.

europe.label: European expert survey
europe.note: A different panel of academics, a different questionnaire and a different scale, across 28 European countries, 1999 to 2024. It is carried because it agrees: economic distance moved +0% over those twenty-five years against +38% on liberal and traditional values. CHES.

society.label: Society
society.note: Not a spread across parties: one expert rating of whether the public itself is split into camps. V-Dem, 176 countries.

axes.label: Society in antagonistic camps
axes.note: V-Dem asks its country experts whether supporters of opposing political camps interact only within their own group. 0 is none, 4 is a society split in two.

axes.label: Political violence by citizens
axes.note: Whether ordinary citizens use violence to pursue political goals.

sources.name: V-Party v2
sources.detail: Country-Party-Date file, version 2, published February 2022, with a codebook and party coding units. Policy positions and organisational structures of political parties: 3,467 parties across 178 countries and 3,151 elections, 1900 to 2019.

sources.name: Chapel Hill Expert Survey, Europe trend file
sources.publisher: Bakker, Hooghe, Jolly, Marks, Polk and others
sources.detail: Seven waves merged into one file: 1999, 2002, 2006, 2010, 2014, 2019 and 2024. The survey ran in 14 Western European countries and 143 parties in the first wave and in 31 countries and 279 parties in the last, which covers every EU member state plus Iceland, Norway, Switzerland and Turkey.

sources.name: V-Dem v16
sources.detail: Country-Year Full+Others, version 16, published March 2026: 531 V-Dem indicators and 251 indices, plus 62 indicators drawn from other datasets. This page reads one of them, v2cacamps, whose codebook question is “Is society polarized into antagonistic, political camps?” It is rated for 180 countries across 19,333 country-years, 1900 to 2025.
